renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: A lamp shows a room the way its rays show the lamp and the sun shows the day — by power you know Śiva the same way. He carries a trident and wears a skull, yet he has no direction, no place, no time, nothing you can point to and name.

So the goddess begs the real question: what is his full-formed state, and which door leads in? Tell it true. It starts with breath — breath above, life below, an outpouring — held full at the two places where breathings begin.

Wind inside and wind outside stop turning their sky-pair, and by the goddess his form shows. The blossomed power neither goes out nor comes in — thoughtless in the middle, and that is his form. Whatever breath you stretch — breathed out, breathed in, or held — its end is calm, and calm shines by power.

Watch her from the root's shining up to the subtler-than-subtle, held at the twelve-end: she calms, and Bhairava rises. She climbs like lightning, wheel by wheel, three fists up — then past the end, the great rising.
Run the twelve-step course, twelve letters split out, through gross and subtle and highest — and at the end, set free: Śiva.

renders.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms.

paragraphs.text: Lamp shows the room the way rays show the lamp and sun shows the day — power is how you clock Śiva. Trident in hand, skull on deck, and still: no location, no slot, no timestamp, no label that sticks.

So the goddess asks the only question: what is his full form and which door opens it. Say it straight. It starts with breath — breath up top, life down low, the pour-out kind — parked full at the two spots where breaths are born.

Inside wind and outside wind quit turning their sky-pair and she shows his form. The power in bloom neither leaves nor enters — blank in the middle, and that blank is his form. Any breath-phase you stretch to its end lands in calm, and calm shines on power.
Track her from the root-glow up to the subtle-of-subtle, pinned at the twelve-end: she settles, Bhairava rises. Lightning climb, wheel to wheel, three fists up — then past it all, the big rising.
Twelve steps, twelve letters, gross to subtle to supreme — run it clean and walk out free: Śiva.
